title: Lasagna Bolognese
description:
Usually when we make the regular Bolognese sauce for having with pasta, we try to make plenty extra (the sauce freezes well) to have a quick meal later or to use this tasty meat sauce when making a wonderful Lasagna.
I like this Lasagna much better than some of the more traditional ones that are heavy on tomato sauce and mozzarella cheese (despite loving both of those ingredients).
Here you get to enjoy not only the Bolognese but the multiple layers of pasta richly flavored with the luscious Béchamel sauce.
If you don’t happen to eat all of this the first night, it tastes and looks really great the next day…even cold!
START TO FINISH: 1 ½ HOURS
Lasagna Bolognese
Gradually whisk in milk; increase heat to medium-high and bring to full boil, whisking frequently.
Add salt, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, making sure to scrape the bottom and corners of the saucepan.
While the sauce is simmering, put the pasta sheets in the boiling water (two or three at a time) for about 10 minutes.
The sauce will become velvety as it finishes and you’ll have a bit more than 3 cups.
Let cool.
Mix about ¾ cup of the Béchamel sauce into the Bolognese sauce.
Butter or spray an ovenproof baking disk (9 x 13 inches) and spread a very thin layer of the Béchamel sauce on the bottom.
Line the bottom with the pasta pieces covering the whole surface of the dish without overlapping.
Spread ¼ cup or so of the Béchamel-enriched meat sauce over the noodles. Drizzle ¼ cup of Béchamel sauce evenly over the meat sauce. Sprinkle ¼ cup of Parmesan evenly over all.
Repeat layering of noodles, enriched meat sauce, Béchamel sauce, and Parmesan until you’re almost out of ingredients (4-8 layers).
ingredients: First, put some water (with a little salt) on to boil for the pasta
directions: For the Béchamel sauce, melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat until foaming.
Add the flour and cook, whisking constantly, until thoroughly combined, about 1 ½ minutes; mixture shouldn’t brown.
Remove the lasagna from the boiling water when done (maybe a little al dente) and place on wax paper to prevent sticking together.
The final, top layer should be noodles, Béchamel (more than just a drizzle and smoothed), and Parmesan.
Spray a large sheet of foil with oil and cover lasagna (oiled side down). Bake until bubbling, about 30 minutes.
Remove foil, increase heat to 450 and continue to bake until the surface is spotty brown, about 15 minutes (you may need to turn on the broiler the last few minutes).
